title: phat-controller per-repo budget file
description: Per-repo failure budget for the autometta pass-2 autonomous loop. Stored at state/budget.json in the repo it governs. Read on every tick; any cap exhaustion halts the loop for this repo without retry. Per memory/decision-failure-budget-clock-tick.md, the clock-tick count is the primary safety; token and wall-clock caps are secondary belt-and-braces.

token_cap_total.description: This repo's own hard cap on total tokens consumed by workers and verifiers dispatched against it. Optional since card 47, and absent means inherit rather than unlimited: scripts/budget.sh resolves the cap that binds as active drain, then this field, then token_cap_total in the controller config.yaml, then the AUTOMETTA_TOKEN_CAP_FLOOR floor. Set it only where this repo genuinely differs from the host default; the fleet once carried four different numbers here with nothing recording why any of them held. Tick halts when tokens_spent >= the resolved cap.

tokens_spent.description: Tokens consumed so far. Updated by tick.sh after each dispatched process returns and reports usage.

wall_clock_cap_seconds.description: Hard cap on cumulative wall-clock seconds spent inside dispatched processes. Tick halts when wall_clock_elapsed_seconds >= cap.

wall_clock_elapsed_seconds.description: Cumulative wall-clock seconds spent in dispatched processes so far.

clock_tick_cap.description: Primary safety. Maximum number of WORK ticks the controller may consume on this repo. Halt when clock_ticks_used >= cap. Bounds wall-clock independent of how expensive individual workers were. It does not bound polling: see idle_tick_cap.

clock_ticks_used.description: Number of ticks that have done work on this repo: supervised a stage in flight, reaped or killed an agent, transitioned a stage, or dispatched a queued one. A tick that finds nothing to do charges idle_ticks_used instead. Until 2026-08-23 this counter was advanced on the unconditional fall-through at the end of every per-repo tick, so an idle repo reached its cap on a fixed schedule: five of six enabled subscribers were halted on tick-cap having spent zero tokens and zero seconds.

idle_ticks_used.description: Number of ticks that found nothing to do -- no stage in flight and nothing pending. An odometer, not a cap: it answers how much of the window went on polling an empty queue, and halts nothing unless idle_tick_cap is set. Zeroed at the window boundary alongside the other counters. Absent on a budget file predating this field; treat as zero.

idle_tick_cap.description: Optional bound on idle polling, halting with idle-tick-cap when idle_ticks_used >= cap. Absent (the default) means idle polling is unbounded, which is deliberate: an empty queue is not a fault, and a cap whose only reachable effect is to halt an idle repo converts 'nothing to do' into 'cannot work when there is'. Set it only where a repo polling an empty queue is itself the thing to catch.

consecutive_failure_cap.description: Maximum back-to-back verifier-FAIL or stall results tolerated before the loop halts for the repo.

consecutive_failures.description: Current consecutive failure count. Resets to zero on any verifier PASS.

halted.description: Mirror of state.yaml.halted. Set when any cap is exhausted. tick.sh sets this before exiting; subsequent ticks read it and exit immediately.

lifetime_tokens_spent.description: Monotonic total tokens ever charged to this repo. Incremented alongside tokens_spent and never reset, including by the window reset. tokens_spent answers how much of the current window's cap remains; this answers what the repo has actually cost. Absent on a budget file predating this field; treat as unknown, not zero.

halt_reason.description: Which cap exhausted. One of: token-cap | wall-clock-cap | tick-cap | idle-tick-cap | failure-cap, or an operational reason (yq-missing, state-corrupt, invalid-stage-id, operator-*). The first hit only; see halt_reasons for the full set. Null until halted is true.

halt_reasons.description: Every cap that was over on the read that halted the loop, in priority order. halt_reason is its first element. Recorded separately because the caps are tested in a fixed order and the first match used to be the only one written: emergence-lab-gpu halted with clock_ticks_used 470 against a clock_tick_cap of 400 and the file said only token-cap, so the tick breach was never surfaced.

breaches.description: Append-only record of cap breaches, oldest first, bounded to the most recent 50. Written both when a cap halts the loop and, crucially, immediately before budget_ensure_window zeroes the counters at a window boundary. Without it a breach leaves no trace once the window rolls: the counters that prove it are exactly the ones the reset clears.

cleared_by.description: halt: recorded as the loop latched. window-reset: recorded as the daily reset was about to erase the counters. reset-halt: recorded as an operator's `tick.sh --reset-halt` was about to erase them.

token_cap_total.description: The cap that actually bound at the moment of the breach, after resolution: a drain, this repo's own cap, the host default, or the floor.

halted_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the halt was triggered.

halt_logged_at.description: Unix epoch seconds of the last time tick.sh emitted the 'reason already recorded' log line for the current halt_reason. Used to dedupe the halt-log spam, at most once per PHAT_CONTROLLER_HALT_LOG_INTERVAL seconds (default 3600). Cleared by budget_halt so a fresh halt always logs immediately.

halt_logged_reason.description: The halt_reason value halt_logged_at corresponds to. A reason change always logs immediately regardless of the interval.

dash_active_at.description: Unix epoch seconds of the last tick where current_stage was non-null. Stamped by tick.sh's ensure_tmux_viewer, read by its idle-dash reaper to decide whether an autometta-<slug> tmux session has been idle (no in-flight stage) for more than PHAT_CONTROLLER_DASH_IDLE_HOURS (default 24). last_tick_at and tick_count advance on every tick regardless of dispatch, so state.yaml's own mtime is not a usable idle signal; this field is written only when a stage is genuinely in flight.

paused_until.description: Epoch seconds until which dispatch is suspended because the provider refused for a limit reason (subscription window exhausted, 429, overload). A pause is not a halt: no cap was breached, no stage failed, and the loop resumes by itself once the clock passes this value. Ticks still fire and still perform bookkeeping while paused; they simply do not dispatch. Null when not paused.

paused_reason.description: The provider refusal line that caused the pause, recorded verbatim for the dashboard and the operator. Null when not paused.

window_started_at.description: UTC calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the current run window. tick.sh compares this to today's date at the start of every tick; a mismatch means a new window has begun, so a halted-or-at-cap budget is auto-reset (all counters zeroed, caps unchanged, halted cleared) instead of staying terminal across windows. consecutive_failures resets only at this boundary -- the failure cap still halts mid-window. Null on a budget file predating this field; treated as always-a-new-window until first written.
